entries.head: show up

senses.en: to arrive at work or an event

example.en: He showed up forty minutes late with coffee for nobody.
example.zh: 他迟到四十分钟，还只给自己买了咖啡。

entries.l1_note: 到岗是 show up / turn up，不是 appear at work（太书面）。

entries.head: take on

senses.en: to accept extra work or responsibility

example.en: Don't take on another project until this one ships.
example.zh: 这个项目上线前别再接新活了。

entries.l1_note: 承担用 take on；take up 是占用时间或开始爱好。

entries.head: fill in for

senses.en: to do someone's job while they are away

example.en: Can you fill in for me on Friday? My kid has a fever.
example.zh: 周五能替我一下吗？孩子发烧了。

entries.l1_note: 替班是 fill in for；fill out 是填表。

entries.head: step in

senses.en: to get involved to help solve a problem

example.en: My manager stepped in before the argument got worse.
example.zh: 经理在吵起来之前出面了。

entries.l1_note: 介入是 step in；step up 是挺身承担。

entries.head: pitch in

senses.en: to help with a shared task

example.en: Everyone pitched in to get the deck done by six.
example.zh: 大家一起动手，六点前把方案做完了。

entries.l1_note: 搭把手是 pitch in；凑钱是 chip in，差一个字母。

entries.head: get ahead

senses.en: to become more successful than others

example.en: She got ahead by taking the projects nobody wanted.
example.zh: 她靠接没人要的项目走在了前面。

entries.l1_note: 出人头地是 get ahead；get ahead of 是抢在某人前面。

entries.head: keep up

senses.en: to stay at the same pace as the work

example.en: I can't keep up with these ticket requests.
example.zh: 这些工单我跟不上了。

entries.l1_note: 跟得上用 keep up (with)；跟上司无关。

entries.head: step down

example.en: The director stepped down after the audit.
example.zh: 审计之后总监卸任了。

entries.l1_note: 卸任是 step down；step aside 是让位给别人。

entries.head: move up

example.en: He moved up to team lead after two years.
example.zh: 两年后他升成了组长。

entries.l1_note: 升职是 move up / get promoted；move up 也指时间提前。

entries.head: deal with
entries.zh: 把事情解决掉；处理情绪；涉及（话题）

senses.en: to take action on a problem

example.en: I'll deal with the vendor emails this afternoon.
example.zh: 供应商的邮件我下午处理。

example.en: She's still learning how to deal with stress at work.
example.zh: 她还在学着怎么处理工作压力。

example.en: The second chapter deals with refunds and returns.
example.zh: 第二章讲退款和退货。

entries.l1_note: 处理是 deal with，不是 deal（少了 with）。

entries.head: sit down with

senses.en: to have a serious conversation with someone

example.en: I need to sit down with my manager about the workload.
example.zh: 我得跟经理坐下来谈谈工作量。

entries.l1_note: 坐下来谈是 sit down with；不是 sit with（那只是坐一起）。

entries.head: report back

example.en: Report back by Thursday and we'll decide Friday.
example.zh: 周四前汇报，我们周五定。

entries.l1_note: 汇报是 report back (to)，不是 report to（那是上级）。

entries.head: draw up

example.en: Legal is drawing up the contract now.
example.zh: 法务正在起草合同。

entries.l1_note: 起草是 draw up；draw 单独是画。

entries.head: write up

senses.en: to write a full report from notes

example.en: Can you write up the meeting notes today?
example.zh: 今天的会议纪要你能整理出来吗？

entries.l1_note: 整理成文是 write up；write down 是随手记下。

entries.head: type up

senses.zh: 把纸面内容打成电子版
senses.en: to type something written by hand

example.en: I'll type up my notes before the call.
example.zh: 开会前我把笔记打出来。

entries.l1_note: 打字成稿是 type up；type 单独是打字动作。

entries.head: file away

senses.en: to store documents in their proper place

example.en: File away the signed copies and keep one at your desk.
example.zh: 签好的那份归档，桌上留一份。

entries.l1_note: 归档是 file away；file 单独是提交（file a report）。

entries.head: work through

senses.en: to deal with things one by one until finished

example.en: I'm working through the backlog this week.
example.zh: 这周我在清理积压的活。

entries.l1_note: 逐个处理是 work through；work out 是想明白。

entries.head: knuckle down

example.en: We need to knuckle down if we want this by Friday.
example.zh: 想周五交出来，就得收心干活了。

entries.l1_note: 埋头干是 knuckle down；不是“跪下”。

entries.head: buckle down

example.en: She buckled down and finished the report in one night.
example.zh: 她一晚上认真把报告写完了。

entries.l1_note: buckle down 和 knuckle down 同义，美式都常用。

entries.head: slave away

senses.en: to work very hard for a long time

example.en: I've been slaving away on this deck all week.
example.zh: 这一周我都在死磕这份方案。

entries.l1_note: slave away 带抱怨色彩，别对老板说。

entries.head: slog away

senses.en: to keep working hard on something boring

example.en: He slogged away at the spreadsheet till midnight.
example.zh: 他对着表格干到半夜。

entries.l1_note: slog away 强调枯燥，slave away 强调被使唤。

entries.head: churn out

senses.en: to produce a lot of something quickly, often badly

example.en: The team churns out ten posts a day now.
example.zh: 团队现在一天能出十篇稿子。

entries.l1_note: churn out 暗示质量一般，夸人别用。

entries.head: crank out

example.en: We cranked out three versions before lunch.
example.zh: 午饭前我们赶出了三个版本。

entries.l1_note: crank out 比 churn out 少一点贬义，仍是“赶工”。

entries.head: farm out

senses.en: to give work to another company or person

example.en: We farmed out the design work to a studio in Chengdu.
example.zh: 设计我们外包给成都一家工作室了。

entries.l1_note: 外包是 farm out；不是 outsource out（重复）。

entries.head: contract out

senses.en: to arrange for another company to do work

example.en: The cleaning was contracted out last year.
example.zh: 保洁去年就外包出去了。

entries.l1_note: contract out 比 farm out 正式，常见于合同语境。

entries.head: head up

senses.en: to lead a team or project

example.en: She's heading up the new Shanghai office.
example.zh: 她负责新成立的上海办公室。

entries.l1_note: 牵头是 head up；head for 是前往。

entries.head: get down to

example.en: Let's get down to the budget numbers.
example.zh: 我们直接进预算数字吧。

entries.l1_note: 进入正题是 get down to (business/work)。

entries.head: close out

senses.en: to finish a project or account completely

example.en: We closed out the quarter with two open tickets.
example.zh: 这个季度收尾时还剩两个工单。

entries.l1_note: 结项是 close out；close down 是关门停业。

entries.head: hand off

senses.en: to pass responsibility to someone else

example.en: I'll hand off the account to you when I leave.
example.zh: 我走的时候把客户交接给你。

entries.l1_note: hand off 是交接；hand over 更强调移交实物或权力。

entries.head: sign on

senses.en: to join a company or agree to work

example.en: Three new engineers signed on this month.
example.zh: 这个月入职了三个新工程师。

entries.l1_note: 入职是 sign on / come on board；sign in 是签到。

entries.head: carry on

example.en: Sorry for the noise — carry on with your call.
example.zh: 不好意思吵到你了，你继续打电话。

example.en: The team carried on with the launch after the power outage.
example.zh: 停电之后团队还是照常推进发布。

entries.l1_note: carry on 后面直接跟动作：carry on working；不要加 to。

entries.head: team up

senses.en: to join with someone to do something

example.en: Let's team up with the design team on this launch.
example.zh: 这次发布我们跟设计组一起做吧。

entries.l1_note: team up with someone，不是 team up someone；介词 with 不能省。

entries.head: come forward

example.en: No one came forward with the missing receipt.
example.zh: 没人站出来交出那张丢失的发票。

entries.l1_note: come forward 是不及物，别加宾语；要说 come forward with something。

entries.head: take time off

senses.en: to spend time away from work

example.en: I'm taking two days off to move apartments.
example.zh: 我请两天假搬家。

entries.l1_note: take time off 是固定说法；请假条不是 take a leave off。

entries.head: take notice of

example.en: The manager took notice of her extra work.
example.zh: 经理注意到了她的额外付出。

entries.l1_note: take notice of 是注意到；take note of 更正式。

entries.head: keep someone in the dark

senses.en: to not tell someone important information

example.en: They kept the staff in the dark about the layoffs.
example.zh: 裁员的事他们一直瞒着员工。

entries.l1_note: keep someone in the dark about something；不是“把人关在黑屋里”。

entries.head: start off on the right foot
entries.ipa: ˈstɑrt ɔf ɑn ðə raɪt fʊt

senses.en: to begin something in a positive way

example.en: A clear first meeting helps the project start off on the right foot.
example.zh: 第一次会开清楚，项目就能开个好头。

entries.l1_note: start off on the right foot 是“开个好头”；反义是 get off on the wrong foot。
confusables: get off on the wrong foot
collocations: start off on the right foot

entries.head: bend over backward

senses.en: to try very hard to help someone

example.en: The support team bent over backward to fix my account.
example.zh: 客服团队竭尽全力帮我恢复账号。

entries.l1_note: bend over backward 是“竭尽全力帮忙”；不是“向后弯腰”的字面意思。

entries.head: writing on the wall

senses.en: a sign that something bad will happen

example.en: The falling sales are writing on the wall for the old model.
example.zh: 销量下滑对旧款来说是不祥之兆。

entries.l1_note: the writing is on the wall 是“不祥之兆”；常省略 the writing。
collocations: the writing is on the wall
see the writing on the wall

entries.head: adhere to

example.en: All staff must adhere to the safety policy.
example.zh: 所有员工都必须遵守安全政策。

entries.l1_note: adhere to 比 follow 正式；to 是介词。

entries.head: answer for

example.en: Someone has to answer for this mistake.
example.zh: 这个错误得有人负责。

entries.l1_note: answer for + 错误/行为；不是“回答”。

entries.head: attend to

example.en: I'll attend to the client's request after lunch.
example.zh: 午饭后我来处理客户的请求。

entries.l1_note: attend to 是处理/照料；attend 单独用是出席。

entries.head: come under

example.en: The team came under pressure to cut costs.
example.zh: 团队面临削减成本的压力。

entries.l1_note: come under + 压力/审查/管理；不是“在下面”。

entries.head: enter into

example.en: The two sides entered into an agreement.
example.zh: 双方达成了一项协议。

entries.l1_note: enter into an agreement/contract；不是“走进”。

entries.head: frown on

example.en: The company frowns on personal calls at work.
example.zh: 公司不赞成上班打私人电话。

entries.l1_note: frown on/upon + 行为；不是“皱眉”。

entries.head: impact on

example.en: The new policy will impact on everyone.
example.zh: 新政策会影响每个人。

entries.l1_note: impact on + 对象；impact 也可直接带宾语。

entries.head: impose on

example.en: Don't impose your schedule on the whole team.
example.zh: 别把你的时间安排强加给整个团队。

entries.l1_note: impose something on someone；不是“放在上面”。

entries.head: improve on

example.en: It's hard to improve on that design.
example.zh: 那个设计很难再改进了。

entries.l1_note: improve on + 已有事物；不是 improve。

entries.head: meet with

example.en: I'll meet with the client on Friday.
example.zh: 我周五见客户。

entries.l1_note: meet with someone 是会见；meet with a problem 是遇到问题。

entries.head: start on

example.en: I'll start on the report after lunch.
example.zh: 午饭后我开始写报告。

entries.l1_note: start on + 任务；start 单独用是开始。

entries.head: butter up

example.en: He tried to butter up the manager before the review.
example.zh: 评审前他想讨好经理。

entries.l1_note: butter someone up 是讨好；不是“涂黄油”。

entries.head: crack down

example.en: The company is cracking down on late submissions.
example.zh: 公司正在严查迟交。

entries.l1_note: crack down on + 行为；不是“裂开”。

entries.head: do away with

example.en: They did away with the paper timesheet.
example.zh: 他们废除了纸质考勤表。

entries.l1_note: do away with + 制度/东西；不是“带走”。

entries.head: drum up

example.en: We need to drum up more support for the plan.
example.zh: 我们得为这个计划争取更多支持。

entries.l1_note: drum up + 支持/生意；不是“打鼓”。

entries.head: go beyond

example.en: She went beyond what the client asked for.
example.zh: 她做的超出了客户要求。

entries.l1_note: go beyond + 范围/要求；不是“去那边”。

entries.head: goof up

example.en: I goofed up the file name and sent the wrong version.
example.zh: 我把文件名搞错了，发错了版本。

entries.l1_note: goof up 是搞砸；美式口语。

entries.head: kiss up to

example.en: He's always kissing up to the new director.
example.zh: 他总在拍新总监的马屁。

entries.l1_note: kiss up to someone 是拍马屁；不礼貌。

entries.head: pull together

example.en: The team pulled together to finish the launch.
example.zh: 团队齐心协力完成了发布。

entries.l1_note: pull together 是不及物/及物；不是“拉到一起”的字面义。

entries.head: rush off

example.en: She rushed off to catch the last subway.
example.zh: 她匆匆离开去赶末班地铁。

entries.l1_note: rush off 是不及物；rush off to + 地方。

entries.head: send out

example.en: We sent out the meeting notes this morning.
example.zh: 我们今天上午把会议纪要发出去了。

entries.l1_note: send out + 材料；send 是寄/发。

entries.head: shake up

example.en: The new boss shook up the whole department.
example.zh: 新老板把整个部门大改了一番。

entries.l1_note: shake up + 组织/人；不是“摇匀”。

entries.head: sit back

example.en: Don't just sit back and wait for someone else.
example.zh: 别光坐着等别人。

entries.l1_note: sit back 可指放松，也可指袖手旁观。

entries.head: slack off

example.en: He slacks off whenever the manager is away.
example.zh: 经理一走他就偷懒。

entries.l1_note: slack off 是偷懒；不是“松开”。

entries.head: slip off

example.en: She slipped off before the meeting ended.
example.zh: 会议结束前她溜走了。

entries.l1_note: slip off 是悄悄离开；slip 是滑。

entries.head: stand aside

example.en: He stood aside and let the new manager lead.
example.zh: 他退到一旁，让新经理来带。

entries.l1_note: stand aside 是让开/退居一旁；不是“站在旁边”。

entries.head: step aside

example.en: The director stepped aside after the scandal.
example.zh: 丑闻之后总监让位了。

entries.l1_note: step aside 是让位/退出；不是“走到一边”。

entries.head: suck up to

example.en: He sucks up to anyone with power.
example.zh: 谁有权他就巴结谁。

entries.l1_note: suck up to someone 是巴结；不礼貌。

entries.head: write in

example.en: Several listeners wrote in to complain.
example.zh: 有几个听众写信来投诉。

entries.l1_note: write in 是不及物“写信给机构”；write down 是记下。

entries.head: cozy up

example.en: He's been cozying up to the new director.
example.zh: 他一直在跟新总监套近乎。

entries.l1_note: cozy up to someone 是套近乎；美式口语。

entries.head: be in on

example.en: Are you in on the new hiring plan?
example.zh: 你参与新招聘计划了吗？

entries.l1_note: be in on + 计划/秘密；不是“在里面”。

entries.head: call it a day

example.en: We finished the report, so let's call it a day.
example.zh: 报告写完了，今天收工吧。

entries.l1_note: call it a day 是“今天到此为止”；不是“叫它一天”。

entries.head: have one eye on

example.en: Keep one eye on the clock during the demo.
example.zh: 演示时留意一下时间。

entries.l1_note: have one eye on + 事；不是“一只眼”。

entries.head: get off on the wrong foot
entries.ipa: ɡɛt ˈɔf ɑn ðə ˈrɔŋ fʊt
entries.zh: 一上来就搞砸、开个坏头

senses.zh: 一开始就把关系或事情弄僵
senses.en: to start a relationship or project badly

example.en: I showed up late and got off on the wrong foot with my new manager.
example.zh: 我迟到，跟新经理一上来就把关系弄僵了。

entries.l1_note: 与 start off on the right foot 相对；固定用 on the wrong foot。
confusables: start off on the right foot
collocations: get off on the wrong foot with someone
get off on the wrong foot
